title: Claude-side Engram nudge may be redundant with the harness instruction re-read, and it costs a delivery page
outcome:
TWO INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS MAY TARGET THE SAME CLAUDE COMPACTION BOUNDARY, AND
NOBODY HAS MEASURED WHETHER OURS CONTRIBUTES ANYTHING.

WHAT WE KNOW, from source and from a peer's field observation:

1. TermAl has its own post-compaction mechanism. claude_spawn.rs:884-885 marks
   an Engram context nudge when a Claude event signals compaction;
   turn_dispatch.rs consumes it at the next dispatch by running, through
   engram_mcp_config.rs:402, a REAL command:
     `engram --project-file <..> --home <..> work --actor-id <..>
      --session-id <..> next --context-generation termal-<gen>`
   That is the ADVANCING read (`next`), not `--peek`. EVERY POST-COMPACTION
   DISPATCH THEREFORE CONSUMES A DELIVERY PAGE.

2. The Claude Code harness has its OWN mechanism. A peer observed, in a real
   session, a host block reading "Instruction files were re-read after the
   conversation was compacted; these differ from their earlier copies - each
   replaces its earlier copy", followed by the recovery behaviour. That is the
   model host re-reading instruction files. IT IS NOT OUR NUDGE.

THE PROBLEM IS EVIDENTIAL BEFORE IT IS FUNCTIONAL: if both fire at the same
boundary, then "context came back after compaction" is equally consistent with
ours alone, theirs alone, or both. Any measurement of our nudge's effectiveness
on the Claude family measures the SUM unless the two are separated first. This
is the same confound that invalidated a behavioural test earlier today, one
level up: confounded MECHANISMS rather than confounded stimuli.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND METHOD: our mechanism is not free. It spawns a process
and consumes an Engram delivery page on every post-compaction dispatch. If the
harness's file re-read already restores what the agent needs on the Claude side,
we may be paying that cost for no added recovery - and nobody would notice,
because the outcome looks identical either way. The failure mode here is not an
error; it is a cost with an unmeasured benefit.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, stated as a design note rather than a plan: the two must
be distinguishable at the boundary. Either our injected context carries a marker
that the harness's re-read cannot produce, or a session runs with our nudge
disabled to see whether recovery still occurs. A positive observation without
that separation cannot be credited to us.

NOT AN ASSERTION THAT THE NUDGE IS USELESS. It may be doing essential work,
especially where instruction files do not contain current Engram state at all -
and note the asymmetry: on the CODEX side the file route provably does NOT
refresh across compaction (measured, see tm-rxhl), so there the nudge has no
competitor and is very likely load-bearing. The open question is specifically
the CLAUDE side, where a second mechanism demonstrably exists.

Credit: the two-mechanism observation came from Engram::Fable, who noticed that
his own positive proof identified the harness's re-read and not our nudge.
Related: tm-rxhl carries the Codex-side measurements.
